correctness.rationale: The lower bound is an explicit 120-word packing whose channel balls are reconstructed and checked pairwise disjoint. The verifier implements the channel both by maximal-run shortening and by direct position deletion with distinct-run constraints and checks agreement on all 512 sources. The upper bound is an exact rational weighted-cover certificate of total weight 120; every source ball has weight at least 1. Disjointness then proves any code has at most 120 words. All arithmetic in the certificate replay is exact, and no incomplete search or optimization log is used as a proof.

originality.rationale: The channel-defining 2023 paper was inspected at the definitions, equivalence proposition, main construction statements, and special-case discussion. It does not state the exact length-nine two-run magnitude-one optimum. Targeted exact-value, alias, parameter, broader-coverage, and table searches found no inspected source or published-finding record whose theorem implies the value 120. Nearby work treats different channels or asymptotic constructions. A residual unindexed-computation risk is retained.
residual_risks: A poorly indexed or unpublished finite computation may contain the same length-nine value.
The source paper uses an “at most” definition but later employs compressed error-ball notation; the present finding removes that ambiguity by explicitly stating the at-most channel it proves.

value.rationale: This is the exact maximum cardinality for a central finite packing invariant of the limited-magnitude sticky-deletion model, at a natural first moderate binary instance with two independently affected runs. It supplies a benchmark absent from the inspected construction-focused literature and shows a weighted sphere-packing bound is sharp at this parameter. The parameter is motivated by the primary channel model rather than chosen solely because a computation happened to terminate.
